subject: maths
title: Angle Rules & Parallel Lines
welcome_lead: Now you'll unlock angle relationships — straight lines, vertically opposite, parallel-line rules and exterior polygon angles.
meta_desc: GCSE Maths Geometry — straight-line angles, vertically opposite, alternate/corresponding/co-interior angles, exterior polygon angles.
final_note: You learned straight-line, vertically opposite, parallel-line angle rules and the 360°/n exterior rule.

concepts.def: When two lines cross, opposite angles are equal.
Z-shape on parallel lines — they are equal.
F-shape on parallel lines — they are equal.
C-shape on parallel lines — they add to 180°.
Equals 360° ÷ n, where n = side count.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Angles on a straight line add to 180°.

So if one angle on a line is 130°, the other is 180 − 130 = 50°.

When two straight lines cross, you get an X. The angles opposite each other are equal — these are vertically opposite angles. If one is 70°, the one straight across is also 70°.

When a straight line cuts across two parallel lines, three rules pop up:

• Alternate angles (Z-shape) are equal.
• Corresponding angles (F-shape) are equal.
• Co-interior angles (C-shape) add to 180°.

Example: one alternate angle is 65° → the other is also 65°. One co-interior is 110° → the other is 180 − 110 = 70°.

The exterior angles of any polygon always add to 360°.

For a regular polygon (all sides and angles equal):

Exterior angle = 360° ÷ n

• Regular hexagon (n=6): 360 ÷ 6 = 60°
• Regular octagon (n=8): 360 ÷ 8 = 45°
• Regular decagon (n=10): 360 ÷ 10 = 36°
